chunks: It is narrated from Saad ibn Abdullah from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik from Sayyar ibn Muhammad al-Basri from Ali ibn Umar al-Nuflawi who said:
I was with Abul Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) in his house, when Abu Ja'far passed by him. I asked him: Is he our master? He replied: No. Your master is Hasan.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْعَسْكَرِيُّ: Abul Hasan al-Askari, the tenth Imam
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, often referring to the elder brother of the Imam

ai.seo_question: Who is the master of the Shia according to Imam al-Askari in this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the distinction between the two sons of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), specifically identifying Abu Ja'far as the elder brother who was often in the public eye, while Imam Hasan (the Mahdi) remained the true spiritual authority. The Imam’s clarification underscores the Shia doctrine of the Hidden Imam, where the designated successor is distinguished from his siblings despite their shared lineage and proximity. This incident serves as an early indicator of the eventual occultation, reinforcing the concept of *al-Imam al-Muntazar* (the Awaited Imam).

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 163 - It is narrated from Saad bin Abdullah from Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Malik from Sayyar bin Muhammad Basri from Ali bin Umar Naufali that he said:
I was with Abul Hasan Askari [Imam Hadi (a.s)] in his house, when Abu Ja’far passed from there. I asked: Is he our master? He replied: No, your master is Hasan.
